title: Spotlight Fallacy
description: Assuming that the media’s coverage of a certain class or category is representative of the class or category in whole.
logical_form:
The media have been covering X quite a bit by describing it as Y.

Therefore, X can be described as Y.

examples.example: It seems like we are constantly hearing about crimes committed on our streets.  America is a very dangerous place.
examples.explanation: The media reports on stories of interest, which include crimes.  It does not report on all the non-crimes.  Assuming from this, “American is a very dangerous place” is fallacious reasoning.

examples.example: I am seeing more and more miracles being reported on respectable news programs.  The other day there was a story about a guy who had trouble walking, prayed to the recently deceased Pope, now walks just fine!  Miracles are all around us!
examples.explanation: People love stories of hope and miracles.  You won’t find stories about how someone prayed to be healed then died.  These are not the kind of stories that attract viewers and sell papers.  As a result, the spotlight fallacy makes us think the rare cases, almost certainly due to normal and necessary statistical fluctuations, seem like the norm.  Believing that they are, is fallacious reasoning.

exceptions: Complete coverage of a small, manageable class, by an unbiased media outlet, may accurately be representative of the entire class.
tips: Be very selective of the types of “news” programs you watch.
references: Tanner, K. (2013). Common Nonsense Based on Faulty Appeals. In *Common Sense* (pp. 31–43). Apress. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4302-4153-9_3
description_et: Eeldusel, et teatud klassi või kategooria kajastus meedias esindab klassi või kategooriat tervikuna.
logical_form_et:
Meedia on X-i üsna palju kajastanud, kirjeldades seda kui Y.

Seetõttu võib X-i kirjeldada kui Y.
exceptions_et: Väikese ja hallatava klassi täielik kajastus erapooletu meediaväljaande poolt võib täpselt esindada kogu klassi.
tips_et: Olge väga valiv seda tüüpi uudistesaadete osas, mida vaatate.

examples_et.example: Tundub, et kuuleme pidevalt meie tänavatel toime pandud kuritegudest.  Ameerika on väga ohtlik koht.
examples_et.explanation: Meedia kajastab huvitavaid lugusid, mis hõlmavad kuritegusid.  See ei kajasta kõiki mittekuritegusid.  Sellest lähtuvalt eeldades, et "Ameerika on väga ohtlik koht" on ekslik arutluskäik.
examples_et.original_example: It seems like we are constantly hearing about crimes committed on our streets.  America is a very dangerous place.
examples_et.original_explanation: The media reports on stories of interest, which include crimes.  It does not report on all the non-crimes.  Assuming from this, “American is a very dangerous place” is fallacious reasoning.

examples_et.example: Näen, et auväärsetes uudistesaadetes kajastatakse üha rohkem imesid.  Teisel päeval oli lugu ühest tüübist, kellel oli raskusi kõndimisega, palvetas hiljuti surnud paavsti poole, nüüd kõnnib hästi!  Imed on kõikjal meie ümber!
examples_et.explanation: Inimestele meeldivad lood lootusest ja imedest.  Te ei leia lugusid selle kohta, kuidas keegi palvetas, et saada terveks, kuid suri.  Need ei ole sellised lood, mis vaatajaid köidavad ja pabereid müüvad.  Selle tulemusena paneb prožektorite eksitus meid arvama, et harvad juhtumid, mis on peaaegu kindlasti tingitud normaalsetest ja vajalikest statistilistest kõikumistest, tunduvad normina.  Uskuda, et nad nii on, on ekslik arutluskäik.
